narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed morning despite European equity strength. The index sits in a technical no-man's-land: still in bull mode 4.4% above its 200-day MA, but the weak ADX (10.7) and MACD below signal strip conviction from the move. VIX's 3.84% jump signals underlying risk-off despite positive open—geopolitical headlines around Ukraine energy infrastructure and NATO tensions are creating friction. USD/SEK strength (+0.56%) should help exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson), but this is offset by oil's sharp rally (+1.84%), which pressures industrial input costs and consumer spending. Copper's 1.78% gain and oil strength favor Boliden, but broad technicals remain cautious with RSI at 41.7 (neutral) and the index just 1.9% from its 52-week high.
morningBrief: Open with caution. European peers showing modest green but OMX30 technicals lack follow-through—ADX below 18 means low conviction on directional moves, so cut typical sector magnitudes by 30%. Watch 3123 (yesterday close); above 3140 targets 3180 (50-MA resistance), below 3100 risks 3085 support. USD/SEK at 10.02 is a tailwind for export names (Volvo B, Atlas Copco A, Ericsson B) but oil's 1.84% spike pressures industrial margins—monitor input cost commentary. Copper +1.78% is a strong Boliden signal; watch for mining rotation into defensives. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) get slight NIM lift from yields steady-ish at 5.24%, but real estate should underperform refinancing pressure. Tech/Telecom faces NASDAQ-flu risk (down -0.18% Friday) and weak ADX—de-risk. Most critical: geopolitical headlines (Ukraine, NATO) have VIX +3.84%; any escalation spikes volatility and kills risk appetite. Watch 14:30 CET US Jobless Claims for transatlantic sentiment.
